How Much Should You Pay for an Item to Resell?

Work backward from the expected sale price and your required return.

The safest sourcing decision starts with a conservative expected selling price and works backward. Subtract selling fees, shipping, preparation costs, and your desired profit. What remains is the most you can pay.

Maximum buy price = expected sale price − selling costs − desired profit

When the goal is ROI instead of a fixed dollar profit, the maximum buy price must also satisfy the return you require. Our maximum buy price calculator handles both approaches.

Use realistic sale prices

Look at comparable completed sales where available, then account for condition, season, competition, and how quickly you need to sell. Asking prices do not prove demand.

Leave a buffer

Unknown defects, returns, extra packing, and price negotiation can erase a thin margin. A sourcing ceiling is a decision boundary, not a prediction or guarantee.

Keep the estimate honest.

Fee structures and actual costs can change. Verify the rules that apply to your sale and treat every result as planning information.
